01

Before you start

Finding the MOD screen

Launch the game, and on the title screen clickWorkshop in the bottom-left corner。

Three buttons

That takes you to the Mod Manager, where each of the three buttons does one job:

Use other people's
Manage Mods

Manage the MODs you have installed (local and Workshop):enable, disable and reorder them. When you have finished building a MOD, this is also where you press Apply Changes to see it in action.

Build your own
Create Mod

Create and edit MOD content.Everything in this guide happens on this one screen — Asset Library, Appearance, Fonts, Music & SFX, Voice, Localization and Edit Equipment are all here.

Find new ones
Mod Store

Browse and subscribe to Steam Workshop MODs from inside the game, without switching to a browser.

Three things to know first

Get these three straight before you start and you will save yourself a lot of backtracking.

FirstTarget package — which MOD you are editing

Every page except Tutorial and Asset Library has aTarget package: selector in the top-right corner. It shows what you are currently editing; everything you save is written into that package. Open it and there is an input field at the bottom —type a new name, press Create, and you have started a new MOD package。

SecondThe page toggle — whether this package covers this kind of content

Every content page has atoggle in the top-left corner (showing Enabled or Disabled). A new package starts with all of them off, so turn on whichever one you are working on. A page that is off has no effect when applied, even if you have set things up on it.

The small dot next to each item in the left-hand list is that page's status:filled = Enabled, hollow = Disabled, so you can see at a glance what a package covers. Toggling one is written to disk by Save Settings in the top-right corner; it does not take effect on its own.

ThirdSaving is not applying

These two are easy to confuse and completely different:

  • Save Settings — writes your edits into the MOD package on disk. Every page has this in the top-right corner.
  • Apply Changes — go to Manage Mods, tick the package and press it; the game reloads on the spot, so youdo not need to restart。

You get a warning if you leave a page, switch target package or close the window with unsaved work. Nine times out of ten, "I saved it but nothing happened" means Apply Changes was never pressed.

02

Asset Library: where your files go

Every file you want to use — fonts, music, voice clips, icons — goes into theAsset Library first. It is one foldershared by every MOD package, stored under the game's save directory.

When you pick an asset on an editing page and pressSave Settings, only the files youactually usedare copied into your MOD package. That is why a published package is always self-contained — nobody downloads it and finds files missing.

You do not need to memorise the path Every tab on the Asset Library page has anOpen folderbutton in the top-right corner that opens Explorer straight at the right place.

If you want to find it yourself, it lives here:

Asset Library locationPaste it into Run (Win + R) and press Enter
%USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\UserJoy\HSLR\ModAssetLibrary\

Inside are seven folders by type, matching the seven tabs across the top of the Asset Library page:

TabFolderWhat goes in it
Sprite sheetsskin\Frame-by-frame animation sheets for battle sprites
Imagesimage\Portrait and avatar artwork (PNG / JPG)
Fontsfont\.ttf / .otf
Audiobgm\Background music .mp3 / .wav / .ogg
Voicevoice\Dialogue voice lines .mp3 / .wav / .ogg
Iconsicon\Equipment icons (PNG)
Spinespine\External Spine data, one subfolder per character
Remember to press Rescan after copying files in The list does not refresh by itself. If a file you just copied in is missing, press Rescan in the tab's top-right corner and it will show up.
03

Edit Equipment

Pick a piece of equipment that already exists in the game and change its attributes, magic effects, description and icons. Fields you leave alone keep the game's original values, so only what you actually edited gets overridden.

Step 1Choose a piece of equipment

On the left, clickEdit Equipment, turn onEnable equipment editsin the top-left corner, then pressChoose equipment」。

You can filter by slot (helmet / body / boots / weapon / accessory), or search by name and ID. Whatever you pick joins the list below, where each row can be edited, collapsed or removed, and is labelled withwhat you changed on it。

Leave All / Player / Enemy alone Those three are not equipment slots but thebase stats shared by every unit. Editing them affects every unit in the game — best avoided in an ordinary MOD.

Step 2Pick a data version

The game keeps two sets of equipment data, and the difficulty setting decides which is read:

OptionEffect
Classic + NormalThe default — use this if you are unsure.Both difficulties pick up your edits
Classic onlyOnly players on Classic difficulty see the change
Normal onlyOnly players on Normal difficulty see the change

Step 3Edit the attributes

Attributes the item already has can be edited directly, and every row has aResetto put the game's original value back.

To add an attribute the item never had: pick it from the dropdown, enter a value, and pressAdd attribute」。 You can add at most 5 (changing values the item already had does not count).

The dropdown lists English field names Str is Strength,Speed is Speed,PhysicalAttack is physical attack, and so on. All 41 are explained at the end underThe 41 editable attributes — worth a look before you start.
Negative values are allowed Useful for equipment with a downside — a heavy weapon at +30 attack but −10 speed, say.

Step 4Edit the magic effects

You can remove the item's existing effects one by one, andAdd magic effectlets you pick a passive effect from a list; the game wraps it into an equipment skill and writes it into the MOD for you.

Two things you cannot touch A weapon'snormal attack skill is locked and cannot be removed (without it the weapon cannot attack), and effects that would make a stage unwinnable (undying, no corpse removal) are not offered.

Step 5Edit the description and icons

For the description, just press Enter for a line break; on save it is converted to the game's line-break marker #」——so do not type # yourself. Restore original description undoes any mess.

Icons come in two sizes,IconandBig icon, each replaceable independently. Pick from the Asset Library'sIconstab, or leave it onKeep original」。

Icons go in the Asset Library's Icons tab which is ModAssetLibrary\icon\. You do not have to memorise it — the dialog aboveprints the folder it is reading right under its title. Drop your image at that path, press Pick again, and there it is.

Step 6Save to MOD

Use the preview in theSave to MOD, then apply it in Manage Mods.

Repeated edits never compound Every edit is measured against theoriginal data with no MODs applied, so editing the same item ten times gives exactly the same result as getting it right first time. Remove an item's edits and it goes straight back to the game's original.
04

Apply and publish

Seeing it in game

  1. On the editing page, pressSave Settings」／「Save (top-right corner of every page)
  2. Use< Backin the top-left corner to return to the Mod Manager, then openManage Mods」
  3. Find your package in the Installed MODs list and tickLoaded
  4. Press the redApply Changesbutton in the top-right corner — the game reloads on the spot, so youdo not need to restart
  5. Go back into the game and your work is there
Saved, but nothing changed? Nine times out of ten, Apply Changes was never pressed. Also check that thetop-left page toggleon the page you edited is on, and that the package isticked。

Publishing to the Workshop

The Create Mod page has a redbottom-left cornerbutton in thePublish to Workshop. Publishing runs Save all first, andwhat goes out cannot be taken back, so you get a confirmation dialog. The cover image comes from the package's preview.png。

Finished MODs are yours to upload and share — other players can then subscribe to your work straight from the Workshop.

A

The 41 editable attributes

Edit EquipmentEverything the Add attribute dropdown offers. The dropdown shows English field names, so they are grouped here in dropdown order with their meanings on the right.

GroupName in the dropdown → meaning
Core statsStr Strength,Dex Dexterity,Mind Mind,Con Constitution
Survival and movementMaxHp Max HP,MaxMp Max MP,Defense Defence,Stamina Morale,Speed Speed,Move Movement
AttackPhysicalAttack Physical attack,MagicAttack Magic attack,AttackRange Attack range
ResistancesFireRes Fire resistance,WaterRes Water resistance,AirRes Wind resistance,EarthRes Earth resistance,MindRes Mind resistance,IgnoreResist Resistance ignore
Accuracy and ratesPhysicalHitRatio Physical accuracy,MagicHitRatio Magic accuracy,DodgeRatio Evasion rate,AttackBackRatio Counter rate,CriticalRatio Critical rate,StaminaRatio Morale rate,MpCostRatio MP cost rate
RewardsStealRatio Steal rate,ExpRatio EXP rate,GoldRatio Gold rate
Damage reductionPhysicalDR Physical damage reduction,FireDR Fire damage reduction,WaterDR Water damage reduction,AirDR Wind damage reduction,EarthDR Earth damage reduction,MindDR Mind damage reduction
MultipliersPhysicalRatio Physical multiplier,DefenseRatio Defence multiplier,AtkDamageRatio Attack damage rate,DefDamageRatio Defence damage rate,MaxHPRatio Max HP rate,MaxMPRatio Max MP rate
Anything with "rate" in the name is usually a percentage Entering 10 normally means +10%, not +10 points. Look at what the item's original figures are before you edit, and stay in the same order of magnitude — that is how you avoid building something broken.
B

Troubleshooting

SymptomUsual cause
A file just added to the Asset Library is missing from the editing page's listPress Rescan on that page — the Asset Library page and the editing page each have their own
Settings saved into the wrong packageYou switched target package without going back to reload that page. Check the skipped list that Save all prints
Equipment edited but nothing changed in gameThe difficulty does not match the Data version. When in doubt, pick Classic + Normal
A # appears in the item descriptionYou typed a # in the description yourself. Just press Enter for line breaks
